chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Yahya ibn al-Hajjaj, from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sailor: I carry food with him, then I take possession of it from him, and it is deficient. So he (peace be upon him) said: If he is trustworthy, then do not hold him liable.
ai.seo_question: When is a sailor or carrier not liable for lost or deficient goods?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* under the chapter on commercial liabilities, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a sailor is not automatically liable for minor deficiencies in cargo if he is considered trustworthy (*ma'mun*), distinguishing between natural loss and negligence. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in trade contracts, where liability is contingent upon proven fault rather than strict liability. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the limits of *daman* (guarantee) in maritime and transport commerce.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahman Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Yahya Bin Al Hajjaj, from Khalid Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the sailor who carried foodstuff with him, then I took possession of it from him, and it was deficient’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he was trustworthy, so you should not hold him liable’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Yahya ibn al-Hajjaj from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who transported people on the water to the other side and I carried foodstuff through him then received it from him and it was reduced.
He (the Imam) said, ‘If he is trusted, you must not hold him liable.’”
